clue.text: City detective in supermarket rejected graduates

indicators.note: something rejected is sent back, so the shop's name is read from its end to its start
one item sits within another, so the detective goes inside the store's name

blocks.note: Asda is a British supermarket chain
two holders of a Bachelor of Arts

explanation.surface: A police officer in a city supermarket turns away a group of recent graduates.
explanation.walkthrough: Asda is a British supermarket chain. 'Rejected' applies only to the store, not to the graduates that follow.
explanation.definitionFit: Addis Ababa is the capital of Ethiopia, so it is an example of a city.

clue.text: Description of scamp, daily switching sides

indicators.note: the two halves of the word change places, the left half moving to the right

blocks.note: a daily, or char, is a cleaning lady in British usage

explanation.surface: A cleaner who changes sides while being described as a rascal.
explanation.walkthrough: A daily is British slang for a cleaner, also called a char; swap its halves CH and AR to get ARCH.
explanation.definitionFit: Arch means playfully mischievous, an adjective suited to describing a cheeky scamp.

clue.text: Graze leg during amorous activity in party

indicators.note: something happening during another event falls within it, so one piece goes inside another
the combined pieces are placed within the word for a celebration

blocks.note: it is a euphemism for sex

explanation.surface: Someone grazes their leg while fooling around at a party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Graze' looks like a cut leg, but it is the definition in its browsing sense; the pieces nest three deep.
explanation.definitionFit: To dip into a book is to browse it casually, which is a figurative sense of grazing.

clue.text: Drink a soldier consumes wrongly behind VIPs' bar close to waterfront

indicators.note: the close of a word is its end, so only its final letter is used
bar here means except, so that letter is excluded from the word for celebrities
to consume is to take inside, so the soldier word swallows the other piece
in a down clue behind means coming after, so the soldier part follows

blocks.note: ill as an adverb means badly or wrongly

explanation.surface: A soldier drinks badly after leaving a celebrity bar near the harbour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bar' looks like a pub for VIPs, but it means except, removing a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Sarsaparilla is a soft drink flavoured with the root of a tropical plant.

clue.text: Buff cups on office tray?

blocks.note: a tray for incoming office papers

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether a polished cup belongs in the office tray.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'on' puts the first piece above the second.
explanation.definitionFit: A buff is an enthusiast with expert knowledge, and a brainbox is a very clever, knowledgeable person.

clue.text: Henry maybe overwhelmed by British swimmer

indicators.note: in a down clue, being overwhelmed means sitting beneath, so the other piece comes first

blocks.note: Lenny Henry is a British comedian, so Henry might be Lenny

explanation.surface: Someone called Henry is beaten by a British swimmer in a race.
explanation.walkthrough: Lenny Henry is a well-known British comedian, so 'Henry maybe' indicates his first name.
explanation.definitionFit: A blenny is a small fish, and any fish is a swimmer in crossword terms.

clue.text: Jerk front of wonky Hillman?

indicators.note: the front of a word is its opening letter, which alone is used

blocks.note: the Hillman Imp was a small British car

explanation.surface: Asks whether a lurch is caused by the faulty front end of an old Hillman car.
explanation.walkthrough: The Hillman Imp was a small British car of the 1960s, so Hillman stands for IMP.
explanation.definitionFit: A jerk is a contemptible or feeble person, close to a weakling or coward.

clue.text: Asian king's lifted boring football team

indicators.note: something boring drills through, so the team sits inside the king piece
in a down clue lifted means read upwards, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: a football side has eleven players, and 11 looks like II

explanation.surface: A football club is boring enough for a king to raise it high.
explanation.walkthrough: A football team has eleven players, and the digits 11 look like the letters II. The king is Shakespeare's Lear.
explanation.definitionFit: Israel lies in Western Asia, so an Israeli person is Asian by geography.

clue.text: Reckless for vessel to change direction

indicators.note: one direction letter is swapped for its opposite, right turning into left

explanation.surface: Calls it reckless for a ship to make a sudden turn.
explanation.walkthrough: R and L are the abbreviations for right and left, so changing direction swaps one for the other inside the vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: Profligate means wildly extravagant or dissolute, close to recklessly wasteful.

clue.text: American who checks couple opening country pile nowadays with hesitation

indicators.note: a couple is two, so the first two letters of the word are kept

blocks.note: a pyre is a heap of wood

explanation.surface: Describes a pair moving into a country house in the present day, with some reluctance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pile' looks like a stately home in the country, but it is a heap of firewood.
explanation.definitionFit: Copyreader is the US term for a sub-editor who checks and corrects text before publication.

clue.text: Soft roll lacking that Italian zest

indicators.note: lacking means without, so the Italian word is taken away

explanation.surface: A soft roll without any Italian-style zing.
explanation.definitionFit: Brio is vigour or vivacity, much the same as zest or liveliness.

clue.text: Network influencer internally altered tea time biscuit

indicators.note: one letter inside the word is changed for another, leaving its ends intact

blocks.note: a guide steers or influences others

explanation.surface: A social media influencer changes the timing of their afternoon tea.
explanation.walkthrough: GUIDE has its middle I changed to E, making GUEDE. 'Tea time' looks like one phrase but gives two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Langue de chat, French for cat's tongue, is a thin finger-shaped crisp biscuit.

clue.text: Language tattooist heard?

indicators.note: something heard is taken by its sound rather than its spelling

blocks.note: a tattooist puts ink on skin, so is an inker

explanation.surface: Wonders which language a tattoo artist might have overheard.
explanation.walkthrough: In a non-rhotic British accent, inker and the answer sound the same.
explanation.definitionFit: Inca is sometimes used as a name for Quechua, the tongue of the Inca empire in Peru.

clue.text: Unique eagle perhaps, whopper, swirling

indicators.note: swirling round turns the word about so it is read the other way

blocks.note: an eagle in golf is a score other than par, so a non-par
a whopper is a big lie

explanation.surface: A one-of-a-kind giant eagle circling in the sky.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Eagle' suggests a bird, but it is the golf score of two under par; 'perhaps' shows NON-PAR is one example.
explanation.definitionFit: Nonpareil means having no equal, matching unique in sense.

clue.text: Person delivering substandard wheel?

blocks.note: a spinner is something that turns, like a wheel

explanation.surface: A delivery driver with a faulty wheel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Delivering' suggests a courier, but it means bowling in cricket.
explanation.definitionFit: An off-spinner is a cricket bowler, and bowling a ball is called a delivery.

clue.text: Hairdo shorn of a tangled mass by Aussie thoroughly

indicators.note: shorn of means stripped of, so a letter is clipped away from the hairstyle

blocks.note: a mat is a tangled mass of hair

explanation.surface: A hairstyle trimmed of a matted knot by an Australian, done thoroughly.
explanation.definitionFit: From A to Z is an idiom meaning completely, covering everything from start to finish.

clue.text: Getting on stage in grisly masks

indicators.note: to mask is to cover over, so the letters lie concealed inside the phrase before it

explanation.surface: An actor getting on stage behind grisly masks.
explanation.definitionFit: Getting on is an idiom for growing old, so it matches the participle.

clue.text: Young Jamie's outside locking kind of light business up

indicators.note: the outside of a name is its first and last letters
in a down clue, up means the word is read from bottom to top
locking in means holding inside, so the outer letters enclose the rest

blocks.note: first and last letters of Jamie
one's line of work is one's business

explanation.surface: A young Jamie outdoors, locking up a lighting business.
explanation.definitionFit: Juvenile means youthful, an adjective for someone not yet adult.

clue.text: Crackling and tripe stuffing poorly chopped

indicators.note: chopped means cut short, so the last letter is lopped off
stuffing goes inside something, so one piece is placed within the other

blocks.note: tat is rubbish, as is tripe

explanation.surface: Pork crackling and tripe stuffing, both badly cut up.
explanation.walkthrough: SICK loses its last letter to make SIC, with TAT inserted.
explanation.definitionFit: Static is the crackling noise heard on a radio from electrical interference.

clue.text: Failure to boot? Server complication ultimately

indicators.note: ultimately means in the end, so only the final letter counts

blocks.note: a Rear Admiral is one who serves in the navy

explanation.surface: A computer that fails to boot up because of a server problem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boot' suggests starting a computer, but to boot means as well.
explanation.definitionFit: An also-ran is an unsuccessful competitor, so it means someone who has failed.

clue.text: Eccentric more than anyone always enriching pursuit

indicators.note: enriching means adding something inside, so one piece goes into the other

blocks.note: e'er is a poetic contraction of ever

explanation.surface: The most eccentric person is forever adding to their search.
explanation.definitionFit: Queer in its old sense means odd, so the superlative means stranger than all others.

clue.text: Character in Argos, another wearing Musk?

indicators.note: something wearing an item has it around them, so one piece is enclosed by the name

blocks.note: another letter of the Greek alphabet, Argos being in Greece

explanation.surface: A character in an Argos shop is wearing a fragrance of musk.
explanation.walkthrough: Argos looks like the British chain store but is the Greek city, so another character there is a Greek letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Epsilon is the fifth letter of the Greek alphabet, and a letter is a character.

clue.text: Reported addict injecting here, wasted?

indicators.note: something reported is passed on by word of mouth, so its sound matters

blocks.note: an addict injects into a vein

explanation.surface: Report of a wasted addict shooting up at this spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wasted' suggests drugged out of one's mind, but it is the definition, meaning to no purpose.
explanation.definitionFit: Effort made in vain is wasted, achieving nothing useful.

clue.text: 1 Down supporter snacked, periodically missing mouth

indicators.note: letters going missing at regular intervals leaves every other one

blocks.note: 1 Down is ARCH, and an insole supports the arch of the foot
second, fourth and sixth letters of snacked

explanation.surface: Someone who snacked occasionally with the mouth unused.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mouth' looks like part of the snacking scene but is the definition; giving mouth is giving cheek.
explanation.definitionFit: Mouth is informal for cheeky backchat, which is impudence or rudeness.

clue.text: Bearing Hoover bags first in storeroom

indicators.note: first means the opening letter of the following word only
to bag is to put in a sack, so one piece is enclosed by the other

blocks.note: to hoover up food is to eat it greedily

explanation.surface: A Hoover vacuum cleaner gets put away in the storeroom.
explanation.walkthrough: Hoover looks like the vacuum cleaner brand but means wolf food down.
explanation.definitionFit: A compass bearing is a direction, and east is one of the four cardinal points.

clue.text: Cork resident at seaside?

blocks.note: first meaning: a stopper that closes something off
second meaning: a marine mammal living on the coast

explanation.walkthrough: Cork suggests the Irish city; with 'resident' it seems to ask for a local, but it is a stopper.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a verb or noun for closing something tight and the name of a flippered sea mammal.

clue.text: Essentially honest, heroic, incendiary?

indicators.note: the essence of a word is its core, so its middle letters are taken

explanation.surface: A character sketch: at heart honest, heroic, and fiery.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks the definition as a hint: legend says the emperor started the Great Fire of Rome.
explanation.definitionFit: Nero was the Roman emperor popularly blamed for burning Rome, hence an arsonist by reputation.

clue.text: Veins visible on this martial artist quite indecent

blocks.note: a dan is a grade of black belt, or its holder

explanation.surface: A martial artist with bulging veins looks rather indecent.
explanation.walkthrough: The veins are not on a body: blue veins run through this cheese.
explanation.definitionFit: Danish Blue is a soft cheese with visible blue veins of mould.

clue.text: African rhino lustful, snubbed

indicators.note: snubbed suggests a stubby nose, so the word loses its tip at the end

explanation.surface: An African rhinoceros, feeling amorous, is rejected.
explanation.walkthrough: Rhino is old British slang for money, so 'African rhino' is a currency, not an animal.
explanation.definitionFit: The rand is the currency of South Africa, and rhino is slang for cash.

clue.text: Fancied tryin' out nearly all of canal section

indicators.note: nearly means not quite complete, so the final letter is dropped

blocks.note: trying out is testing, with the final g dropped as in tryin'

explanation.surface: Someone liked having a go at sailing almost the whole canal stretch.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe in tryin' signals the dropped g carries into TESTIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Intestinal means relating to the intestines, part of the alimentary canal of the gut.
